task.description: Write the regression test for ISS-0457 per WF-03's fail-then-pass rule: this is a fix to EXISTING behavior (scan_for_status/4 already exists and was last-match-wins; ISS-0442 merged before this run's own fix), so the fail-first proof must be shown against the pre-fix code, not against a from-scratch module (the 'code under test does not exist' clause does not apply here). Concretely: (1) build a duplicate-top-level-status fixture -- the one already produced by ISSUE-FIXER in handoffs/WF03-ISS0457-20260904/diagnosis/dup-status-fixture.json is a real, already-demonstrated one; use it or an equivalent you construct the same way. (2) Add a new test asserting that after --autofix, the FIRST depth-1 status occurrence is the one rewritten to its mapped value, and every later depth-1 status occurrence is left byte-identical to its pre-fix value -- the mirror image of ISSUE-FIXER's originally demonstrated divergence. (3) Demonstrate the fail-then-pass property: check out the pre-fix commit (before ELIXIR-DEV's Step 3 change -- main's tip before this run's own commits landed, i.e. commit 373f5363, the ISS-0442 merge commit) in a disposable worktree, run your new test against that commit's code, confirm it FAILS (the old last-match-wins behavior would edit the wrong occurrence), then confirm it PASSES on this run's own branch. Record both real outputs. (4) Update the stale comment block in test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (around lines 722-742) that currently describes this discrepancy as 'deliberately left uncovered' -- since it is now covered, replace that comment with a pointer to the new test and to ISS-0457's resolution, not left describing a now-fixed defect as still-open.
